## Build, verify, and maintain with a coding agent

Today we will improve one report in an existing research repository.

1. Understand the code and the request.
2. Make a focused change with an agent.
3. Check the output and existing tests.
4. Review the diff and leave a handoff.

::: {.notes}
Use docs/lab_meeting/45min_runbook.md. Participants prepare Python or R and an approved client before the presentation. The same short path also works at home. Keep all input and shared screens synthetic.
:::

## Choose your path once

[Python path](https://fritschelab.org/practical-genai-agentic-coding-guide/docs/paths/python/) · [R path](https://fritschelab.org/practical-genai-agentic-coding-guide/docs/paths/r/)

Download the [example repository](https://github.com/FritscheLab/practical-genai-agentic-coding-example) and keep the guide open online.

Both paths use the same six measurements. Follow your path's commands and prompts.

The pipeline already works. We will add a clearer explanation of its exclusions.

::: {.notes}
Open the selected path in the guide. Setup, example runs, verification, review, and handoff remain specific to that language. No model API is needed to run the pipeline.
:::

## Six rows you can explain

| Measurement | Height | Weight | Existing result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| a | 170 | 70 | Keep |
| b | 175 | 70 | Keep |
| c | 180 | 81 | Keep |
| d | Missing | 70 | Exclude: missing height |
| e | 170 | Missing | Exclude: missing weight |
| f | Missing | Missing | Exclude: both |

Each row belongs to a different synthetic person. Dates and BMI values are valid.

## What does a labmate want to know?

**“Why did six input measurements become three?”**

The excluded rows are saved in `outputs/flagged_rows.tsv`.
The summary gives technical totals, but does not explain the reasons.

Open both files before asking for a change.

## Ask the agent to find its way

```text
Read AGENTS.md and REPO_MAP.md. Find the code that writes
summary.md and explain where the excluded rows are available.
Do not edit anything yet. Point to the files you used.
```

Open the files it names. Check its explanation against the six rows.

::: {.notes}
Use the language-specific orientation prompt if preferred. Show the loaded project instructions and effective tool permissions. A confident explanation still needs a check against the files.
:::

## The report we want

```text
3 of 6 input measurements were excluded.

Missing height: 2
Missing weight: 2

Reason counts overlap: one measurement can have both reasons.
```

Why do the reasons add up to four while only three measurements were excluded?

## Give the agent one focused change

Use the implementation prompt in your path.

- Add the readable report using existing exclusion decisions.
- Keep cleaning and data selection the same.
- Run the existing tests and explain the changed files.

Ask for a short plan if the approach is unclear. Then let the agent edit and run commands.

::: {.notes}
The goal is a request learners can understand and check. No new quality threshold, CLI option, or special run status is needed. Discuss new scope before accepting it.
:::

## Verify the result

Run the six-row example again. Read the new summary.

- Three excluded measurements; reason counts two and two.
- Complete-data example: six measurements, no exclusions.
- Existing tests still pass.
- Selected and excluded records stay the same.

Tests and direct inspection answer different questions. Use both.

## Review what changed

```bash
git status --short
git diff
```

Open new files too. Can you explain each change?

A second agent can help review. Check its findings against the code and examples.

## Leave a useful handoff

Ask the agent for a short note:

```text
Summarize what changed, the commands and results we checked,
and anything still unfinished. Include how to rerun the example.
```

Keep the note with the work. Commit reviewed code when you are ready.

## Use the workflow in your own repository

Choose one small improvement whose result you can inspect.

Give the agent context. Verify its work. Leave the next person a clear starting point.
